name: Visual Studio Code
summary: A layered TypeScript workbench that combines platform services, editor and contribution modules, environment-specific entry points, and an extension host connected through an IPC protocol.

features.name: Layered workbench services
features.description: The official source-organization guide describes base, platform, editor, workbench, code, and server layers. Platform services are identified by decorators and provided through an instantiation service, while workbench contributions expose constrained APIs.
benefits: Makes service dependencies explicit and supports delayed or alternate implementations
Allows the workbench to assemble editor and product contributions from modular boundaries
costs: Layer rules and contribution APIs constrain dependency placement
Service registration and lifecycle ownership increase indirection

features.name: Out-of-process extension host
features.description: The official architecture guide states that extensions run in a separate extension-host process. The fixed source establishes an IPC protocol for that process, controls selected process APIs, and includes reconnection and termination handling.
benefits: Separates extension execution and failure handling from the workbench process
Provides a defined protocol boundary for extension API requests and events
costs: Serialization, reconnection, and process lifecycle add latency and failure modes
The boundary cannot eliminate resource contention or extension-level semantic errors

features.name: Multi-environment shared core
features.description: The official guide separates common, browser, Node, Electron, and utility-process targets and describes shared workbench entry points for desktop and web. Environment-specific implementations satisfy the same higher-level service composition where needed.
benefits: Reuses editor and workbench logic across desktop and web deployments
Makes runtime capability constraints visible in source organization
costs: Shared abstractions must accommodate different platform capabilities
Environment-specific substitutions increase build and testing combinations

mathematical_views.question: How do platform services, workbench contributions, editor modules, and target-specific implementations depend on one another?
assumptions: Modules and services are vertices and allowed imports or registrations are directed edges
Layer restrictions are treated as admissibility constraints on edges
The view abstracts bundler behavior, dynamic loading, and the full runtime call graph

mathematical_views.question: How do workbench connection, extension-host readiness, message exchange, reconnection, and termination progress?
assumptions: The extension host and workbench are process states connected by an IPC channel
Ready, connected, disconnected, grace-period, and terminated are abstract protocol states
The model abstracts message payload semantics and operating-system process scheduling

benefits: Explicit service boundaries support modular assembly
costs: Indirection and layer discipline increase integration overhead

benefits: Extension execution is separated by a process and protocol boundary
costs: IPC and reconnection behavior complicate latency and failure reasoning

benefits: A shared core serves desktop and web targets
costs: Platform variation expands implementation and test matrices
